tasks.short: Keep room availability and guest account records.

steps.what: Hold records of room availability the system already keeps.
Compare room availability with the desk list.
Correct guests accounts the clerk checked manually.
Write the accepted correction using computers.

tasks.design: Room availability and guest accounts that {OPS_SYSTEM} already holds stay as they are. The hotel desk clerk compares them with the desk list and corrects a mismatch by hand. {OPS_SYSTEM} writes only that accepted correction.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same availability was kept in a book and typed again into the property system.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system already holds the records, so the clerk only has to correct a mismatch.
tasks.still_hard: Two desks can change the same room, and an account can be wrong for a reason the list does not show.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk decides which mismatch is real. The system does not invent a correction.
tasks.altitude: The records the system already keeps are not a saving. The clerk still finds the mismatch and accepts the correction.

reach.learn: Trust a correction only after the desk clerk has accepted it

evidence.claim: A correction to a stored account can be written from fields the clerk has accepted.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the clerk opens the availability and ends when an accepted correction is stored. Opening a new stay and posting charges stay outside it.
The correction fields are room number or account id, the old value, the new value, and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the new value. A mismatch with no acceptance is not written.
The prior treats the task as automate. The steps disagree: holding the records is existing system work and is not saved clerk labour.
Upkeep is keeping the desk list of rooms that can disagree with the system.
unknowns: How often the desk list still disagrees with the property system.
Who else is allowed to change a guest account.
research_questions: How often does the desk list disagree with the property system?
Who else may change a guest account on the same day?

already_counted.description: Comparing availability with the desk list stays partly in that step

incremental.description: Keep the desk list of rooms that can disagree

approvals.approved_version: account correction the hotel desk clerk accepted after checking it manually

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the desk list has already been retired, the comparison shrinks and the low end is only a rare correction the clerk still has to accept. The records the system already holds are excluded either way. 34 percent is work the system already does and is not saved human labour. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Balance accounts after the nightly audits.

steps.what: Run the nightly audits the system already performs.
Read exceptions from those nightly audits.
Finish bookkeeping by balancing flagged accounts.
File the balancing note the clerk accepted.

tasks.design: The nightly audit that {OPS_SYSTEM} already runs stays as it is. The hotel desk clerk reads the exceptions and does the balancing. {DOCS} files the note the clerk accepted. The audit itself is not treated as clerk time.
tasks.previous_blocker: The audit was a night routine on the property system, and the clerk then retyped the exceptions into a book.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system already produces the audit, so the clerk can read exceptions instead of running the audit again.
tasks.still_hard: An exception can be a real shortage, a timing gap, or a charge the guest will dispute in the morning.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk decides how to balance an exception. The audit does not make that decision.
tasks.altitude: The nightly audit is not time the clerk gets back. Reading exceptions and balancing the flagged accounts stay with the clerk.

reach.learn: Use the balancing note only after the desk clerk has accepted it

evidence.claim: A balancing note can be filed from the exception and the amount the clerk has accepted.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the nightly audit has finished and ends when the accepted balancing note is filed. The audit run itself stays outside the clerk's work.
The note fields are account id, exception amount, the clerk's balancing figure, and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the figure. The audit output is an input, not a saving.
The prior treats the task as automate. The steps disagree: conducting the nightly audit is existing system work and is not saved human labour.
Upkeep is keeping the exception codes the clerk is expected to read.
unknowns: Whether a person still starts the nightly audit by hand at this property.
Which exceptions the clerk may balance without a finance colleague.
research_questions: Does a person still start the nightly audit, or does it already run on its own?
Which exception amounts may the desk balance alone?

already_counted.description: Reading audit exceptions stays inside that step

incremental.description: Keep the exception codes the clerk is expected to read

approvals.approved_version: balancing note the hotel desk clerk accepted after reading the audit

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If a person still has to start the audit, that time is not in this saving and the low end falls further, because only the filing of an accepted note was counted. The audit run stays excluded. 48 percent is work the system already does and is not saved human labour. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compute bills, collect payments, and make change.

steps.what: Compute bills the property system already totals.
Review each computed bill before collection.
Collect payments from guests at the desk.
Make change for guests who paid cash.
Record the payments the clerk collected.

tasks.design: The bill total that {OPS_SYSTEM} already computes stays as it is. The hotel desk clerk reviews it, collects the payment, and makes change. {OPS_SYSTEM} records the payment the clerk collected. It does not take the money.
tasks.previous_blocker: The total was already on the screen, and the clerk retyped the amount after taking the money.
tasks.enabler_now: The property system already totals the bill, so the clerk reviews it and the collected amount can be stored once.
tasks.still_hard: A guest may dispute a line, pay partly in cash, or need a receipt in a form the screen does not show.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk takes the money and makes the change. A stored payment is not the collection.
tasks.altitude: Collecting payments and making change stay at the desk. The bill the system already totals is not a saving.

reach.learn: Count a payment only after the desk clerk has collected it

evidence.claim: A collected amount can be stored against the bill the property system already totaled.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the guest is ready to pay and ends when the collected amount is stored. The bill total the system already computed stays outside the clerk's saving. Refunds stay outside it.
The stored fields are stay id, amount collected, and the clerk's acceptance. The clerk produces the amount by collecting it. The computed bill is an input the system already made.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on collection and change. The bill total is existing system work and is not saved clerk labour.
Upkeep is keeping the payment codes for cash and card.
unknowns: Whether the terminal already records the amount when the card is taken.
How often the guest pays in cash and needs change.
research_questions: Does the card terminal already record the amount on the stay?
What share of desk payments is still cash?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the computed bill stays partly in that step

incremental.description: Keep cash and card payment codes current

approvals.approved_version: payment the hotel desk clerk collected from the guest

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the terminal already records the amount, the write disappears and the low end is the review, the collection, and the change, which stay. The bill the system already totals is excluded either way. 24 percent is work the system already does and is not saved human labour. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Review accounts with guests during check out.

steps.what: Review accounts and charges with guests.
Hear questions during the check out process.
Note a charge the guest accepted at checkout.

tasks.design: The hotel desk clerk reviews the account with the guest and hears their questions. A short note records a charge the guest accepted during that conversation. The conversation is not replaced by a screen.
tasks.previous_blocker: Checkout was already a conversation, and a disputed line was written on the printout afterwards.
tasks.enabler_now: The account is already on the screen, so the clerk can point to it while talking.
tasks.still_hard: The guest may disagree, may be in a hurry, or may need a line explained in the language they speak.
tasks.human_edge: The review with the guest stays with the clerk. A note does not replace that conversation.
tasks.altitude: Almost nothing changes. The clerk still reviews the account with the guest during check out.

reach.learn: Settle the question with the desk clerk, not with a screen alone

evidence.claim: A checkout conversation can sit beside an account the property system already shows.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the guest comes to check out and ends when they leave the desk. Posting new charges and taking payment are separate tasks.
The note, when there is one, is the charge the guest accepted and a short reason. The clerk writes it. Most checkouts need no note.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree. Nothing in the conversation is handed to a model.
Upkeep is small because no new list is required for the conversation itself.
unknowns: How often a guest disputes a line at checkout.
Whether the property already prints the account for the guest.
research_questions: How often does a guest dispute a charge during check out?
Is the account already printed or only on the screen?

already_counted.description: Noting an accepted charge stays mostly in that step

incremental.description: No new list; a rare note uses the charge codes that already exist

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case is the ordinary checkout: the review and the questions stay in full, and the note is rare. The low end is close to the centre because almost none of this time was going to move. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Collecting payments, making change, and reviewing the account with the guest stay. The records, the nightly audit, and the bill total that the system already produces are not treated as time saved. The clerk still accepts a correction, a balancing figure, and a collected payment.
reach: Finance uses a correction or a payment only after the desk clerk has accepted it
skills_to_grow: Reading audit exceptions without treating the audit run as saved work
Accepting an account correction before it is written
Reviewing the bill with the guest during check out
role.ambitious_version: The books the system already keeps stay as they are, and every correction or payment a person relies on is one the desk clerk accepted.
